blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts. At Czarnikow, the IT team helps every office, from London to São Paulo. When your computer has a problem, you can call the help desk or join an online meeting.

In this lesson, A Safe Password, you learn the words you need to talk to IT. A good password is safe and strong. You should not share your password. You should change it sometimes. And you should remember it, so you can log in every day.

You will learn five useful words and practice them in short sentences. Go slowly — one step at a time. Small IT habits today save big problems tomorrow. You can do it!

items.q: Where does the Czarnikow IT team help?
options: Every office, from London to São Paulo
items.why: "the IT team helps every office, from London to São Paulo."

items.q: What can you do when your computer has a problem?
options: Call the help desk or join an online meeting
Share your password with a friend
Turn off the computer and go home
items.why: "you can call the help desk or join an online meeting."

items.q: According to the text, what should you do with your password?
options: Keep it safe and change it sometimes
items.why: "A good password is safe and strong… You should change it sometimes."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which sentence?
options: It is smart to remember your password.
You can call the help desk for help.
A strong password is a good idea.
You should share your password with everyone.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz "You should not share your password" — o autor discorda de compartilhar.

items.q: "Small IT habits today save big problems tomorrow" suggests that…
options: you should change computers every day
simple daily habits help you avoid trouble later
items.why: Inferência: hábitos pequenos e diários (senha segura, etc.) evitam problemas grandes depois.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James explicando a um novo usuário as regras de uma senha segura. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hello, and welcome to Czarnikow! I'm James, from the IT help desk. Today I want to explain the rules for a safe password. It is easy, so please don't worry.

First, your password must be strong. Use letters and numbers together. A strong password is hard to guess, and it keeps your work safe.

Second, never share your password. Not with a friend, not with your manager, not with me. IT will never ask you for it. If someone asks, please call the help desk first.

Third, you should change your password sometimes — maybe every three months. And of course, you must remember it. So choose something you can remember, but other people cannot.

If you forget your password, that is okay. Just call us, and we will help you make a new one. Small habits like this keep the whole company safe. Thank you, and have a good first day!
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Who is speaking, and where does he work?
options: James, from the IT help desk
items.why: "I'm James, from the IT help desk."

items.q: What does James say about a strong password?
options: It uses letters and numbers and is hard to guess
It should be short and easy
It should be the same as your name
items.why: "Use letters and numbers together. A strong password is hard to guess."

items.q: James says you should share your password with…
items.why: "never share your password. Not with a friend, not with your manager, not with me."

items.q: If someone asks for your password, what does James suggest you do?
items.why: Inferência: "IT will never ask you for it. If someone asks, please call the help desk first" — um pedido assim é suspeito.

items.q: How would you best describe James's tone?
options: Friendly and calm, to help a new user
items.why: Inferência: ele diz "please don't worry" e "have a good first day" — é acolhedor e tranquilo.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Your files are safe on the shared drive." Here safe means…
items.why: Safe = seguro, protegido — sem risco.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A good password is ___, so it is hard to guess."
items.why: Strong = forte; uma senha forte é difícil de adivinhar.

items.q: "Please do not share your password with anyone." To share means to…
items.why: Share = compartilhar, dar/mostrar para outra pessoa.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "You should ___ your password every three months."
items.why: Change = trocar; troque a senha de tempos em tempos.

items.q: "I always remember my password, so I never call IT." To remember means to…
items.why: Remember = lembrar, guardar na memória.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs comuns no trabalho e no suporte de TI. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Please log in with your name and password." To log in means to…
options: enter a system with your details
items.why: Log in = entrar num sistema com usuário e senha.

items.q: "IT will help you set up your new laptop." To set up means to…
options: prepare and make it ready to use
items.why: Set up = configurar, deixar pronto para usar.

items.q: "Remember to back up your files every week." To back up means to…
options: make a safe copy of your files
items.why: Back up = fazer uma cópia de segurança.

items.q: "When you finish work, please log out." To log out means to…
options: leave the system and close your session
items.why: Log out = sair do sistema, encerrar a sessão.

items.q: "If you have a problem, please reach out to the help desk." To reach out means to…
items.why: Reach out = entrar em contato, procurar alguém para ajuda.
